auditFix.issue: 전광석화 (電光石火) is a four-character idiom whose lexical meaning is 'as fast as lightning/flint sparks' — speed is baked into the word. Adding the adverb 재빨리 ('quickly') immediately after produces tautological reinforcement: literally 'charged lightning-fast quickly'. Native Korean usage with 전광석화 typically pairs it with verbs of motion alone (전광석화로 돌진했어요 / 전광석화처럼 달려들었어요) without an additional speed adverb.

entries.korean: 이 포켓몬은 껍질에숨기 기술을 익히는 중이에요.
entries.gloss: This Pokémon is learning Withdraw.

auditFix.issue: The official Korean move name 껍질에숨기 contains the internal locative particle 에 ('hide IN [the] shell'). When followed by the object marker 를, learners parse the string as '...껍질에 숨기를...' (two competing clausal readings: '...is in shell, learning to hide...' vs '...is learning [the move] Withdraw'). The double-particle stacking inside a single noun phrase is awkward Korean and causes ambiguity for L2 readers. The previous auditor flagged this as 'uncertain' and no fix was applied; the issue persists.

entries.korean: 체육관 시합에서 PP가 다 떨어져 발버둥을 쳤어요.
entries.gloss: I used Struggle in the gym match.

auditFix.issue: 발버둥 (Struggle) is the auto-triggered fallback move that fires only when a Pokémon has no PP left on any other move. A trainer cannot deliberately '사용하다' Struggle, so '체육관 시합에서 발버둥을 사용했어요' frames an automatic, last-resort move as a chosen tactic. The Korean is grammatical (and 발버둥 also has the everyday meaning 'thrashing/floundering', which makes it superficially read fine), but the in-game collocation is semantically off and atypical of how Korean Pokémon discourse describes Struggle (one would say 발버둥을 쳤어요 / 발버둥치게 됐어요, not 발버둥을 사용했어요).
